title: Stop a glass bottle rolling along the worktop before it goes over the open edge
instruction: Stop the bottle before it rolls off the edge.
context: A bottle knocked over on a sloping drainboard rolls off it and along the worktop towards the open end; most people have lunged for one. If it goes over the edge it smashes. The robot has to read where the bottle is going and how fast, and get a hand into its path in time, then stop it without knocking it off: a moving target, not a placement.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A worktop section (fixed): laminate, 30 cm deep (x 15 to 45) and 55 cm long (y -22.5 to 32.5), its top 6 cm above the table, with an open end at y -22.5 on the robot's right. On its left end a stainless steel drainboard (loose but 15 kg), 30 x 14 cm, from y 18 to 32, sloping 1.2 degrees down towards the right. A 330 ml brown glass beer bottle, full (530 g, 6.1 cm across, 23 cm long), lies on its side on the drainboard at (29, 30), its axis along x and its neck pointing away from the arms; it starts rolling at once and reaches the worktop moving at about 0.25 m/s. Every loose object has friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: 1.0: the bottle still (under 1 cm/s) on the worktop or on the drainboard, lying or stood up, resting on it (not held up off it), having never gone over an edge, held for 1 s, which ends the trial (if time runs out before that has held, it scores 0.9); a hand may stay in front of it. 0: anything else: still rolling, held up, on the table, or over an edge at any point in the trial (recorded as it happens; putting it back doesn't undo it).
reset_notes: Lay the bottle back on its side on the drainboard's high end; it rolls as soon as it is let go.
fidelity: The worktop is a 6 cm block on the table, so going over the edge is a 6 cm drop here, not a real counter's; any fall scores 0. The bottle is a capsule (body and neck) at full size and weight; it rolls straight, where a real bottle's shoulder makes it curve a little. In this simulator a rolling capsule gains a little speed on a level surface once it moves, so a stopped bottle let go of can start rolling again; the task counts a bottle stopped and kept still, with or without a hand in front of it.
